P1.evidence: The only call in the batch with a genuinely pre-qualified setter handoff, and the rep used it correctly — he signalled that he had the notes without letting them replace discovery: 'We've already got quite a bit of context from Kim, but I would love to hear it from you.' He returned to them later to show he had read them: 'I think Kim mentioned something like not being as tight as you used to.' Frame agreement was sought with 'okay?' and given. The open question ran cleanly. The frame itself remains the weak point — 'see if we can actually help you out. If we can, I'll take you a little bit through how I feel like we can fit in there. If not, I'll point you in the right direction' is two parts plus the disqualification clause, with no 'where you are' and no 'what's in the way'.

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch and the only one where sleep and energy were both properly covered. Sleep was explored in real depth — the prospect's account of children waking multiple times nightly was followed up directly with 'do you feel like you're getting more rest now that you can actually go back a lot more into working out?', which produced the genuinely load-bearing answer that the younger child now self-settles. Energy was covered throughout and quantified against a 30-minute walk. Injuries were asked with an explicit question and then scaled 1 to 10, surfacing back pain at 7 daily and 10 at worst. Training history, current frequency, results and diet were all thorough, including fasting windows and 72-hour fasts. Two gaps matter. Occupation was never asked — 'I'm in the fitness industry as well' was volunteered and nothing more was established. And on health conditions, the rep did ask one follow-up about training while medicated, which is more than he managed elsewhere, but he never asked what the infection was, why a PICC line was needed, or whether a physician had cleared him to train; age, height and weight were also volunteered rather than asked.

P3.evidence: By far the best-run Goals phase of the twelve, and the only one where the full depth sequence completed. Aesthetics and function were pinned to numbers — current body fat, target body fat, mobility and endurance each rated. The bridge ran: 'how would that be for you as a person?' The impact question ran and returned real material about naps, energy and cortisol. Crucially the who-else question ran almost verbatim, which the rep skipped on every other call in the batch: 'how do you think that that would impact then when you show up better overall as a partner and also as a dad for them?' It drove straight through to family identity — 'they see the better side of me... oh, dad's happy again... probably makes me less angry as well'. Two accurate reflect-backs ran with explicit confirmation checks. Only the 'something you want to do but can't' question was approximated rather than asked.

P4.evidence: The root-cause work was sharp. Having established the prospect had wanted to change for eighteen months, the rep asked the right question — 'what stopped you from already doing that like a year, one and half years ago?' — and got past the surface answer to sleep deprivation and collapsed energy. He then asked a genuinely good discriminating question that separated the real constraint from the assumed one: 'is it that you don't have the time, or is it that you just hadn't found the right thing for you to do in the time that you did have?' And he tested whether the blocker had actually lifted before proceeding, rather than assuming it. Marked down because prior attempts were never broadly canvassed beyond the gym, and the 'information isn't the problem' challenge was never put.

P5.evidence: Both opening moves ran but the phase did not land, and the rep let it go. The projection was asked properly — 'let's say we sort of don't go for it, and you sort of stay the exact same for the next six months to a year... how would that be for you when nothing really changes?' The prospect deflected it almost entirely: 'if it doesn't, for some miracle, I'd be okay with it, I don't think I'd be too disappointed, it'll be more of like, okay, I didn't push myself hard enough.' Rather than pressing into that, the rep reframed the deflection as a virtue — 'so it sounds like you're not someone to give up' — and then supplied the settle answer himself as a statement to agree with. It got a 'Yeah, no, I would not be okay with that', but the cost of inaction was never actually made real, and no line-in-the-sand question was asked. The close that followed rested on enthusiasm rather than on urgency.

P6.evidence: Correctly sequenced and repeatedly checked. The belief question ran before the presentation began — 'when you have that structure for yourself... and you have someone in your corner, like Trevor... do you feel like you're going to be able to follow through with that?' answered 'Yes, for sure.' It was then re-run after each of the three pillars, each time getting an unqualified yes, and a final pre-close check produced 'Yeah, yeah, definitely' before any number was mentioned. The scripted all-in isolation question was not asked in its proper form; the nearest substitute was 'do you align with the things that I just said on why I feel like it's a good fit?', which is a leading question and drew a non-answer. In practice no blocker existed, so nothing was lost — but the check that would have surfaced one was not run.

P11.evidence: The only call in the batch to complete the phase, and all four steps were attempted. Payment was collected live — $6,000 on a credit card, after a first attempt failed when the prospect closed the tab, with the rep talking him through a retry. The Trevor onboarding was booked on the call for Monday 6 July at 12:15 Pacific and the prospect confirmed both calendar invites arrived. The final step was covered in full and with emphasis: the Skool community link, the welcome email, and the pre-onboarding questionnaire, which the rep pushed to have completed before the Trevor call so the time could be used properly. Only the agreement falls short — the rep described it and asked for it to be signed on receipt, but the email had not arrived by the end of the call, so nothing was signed live as the script requires.

notes: Process-wise the strongest call of the twelve: the setter handoff was used properly, sleep and energy were actually covered, the who-else-does-this-impact question ran and drove through to family identity, the commitment check preceded the presentation, and all four payment and onboarding steps were attempted. No objection of any kind was raised at any point, which is itself worth noting on a $6,000 close and reflects a prospect who arrived pre-sold after two years following the content. Two coaching points stand out despite the outcome. The Consequence Frame was deflected and the rep converted the deflection into a compliment rather than pressing, so the deal rests entirely on enthusiasm. And on the clinical side he asked one screening question, accepted a lay answer, and moved on — the single highest-value correction available here is to treat active medication and a recent PICC line as a stop requiring physician clearance, not as a scheduling advantage.
